 Inside the KOTRA–Chungdam Global Pop-Up Store
Small Korean Brands Take Center Stage in U.S. East Coast Push
Influencers and Shoppers Pack the Store on Opening Day
Visitors Test Cosmetics and Snap Up K-Pop Idol Merchandise
Campaign Targets Black Friday and Christmas, the Biggest Shopping Season
 World | Published 2026.11.15. 06:27:48 | By Yoon Kyoung-hwan ykh22@sedaily.com | Summary | Save A A A Shoppers look around a K-brand pop-up store set up by KOTRA and Korean distributor Chungdam Global at American Dream Mall, a large mixed-use shopping complex in New Jersey, on Nov. 14 local time. New Jersey — Yoon Kyung-hwan, Correspondent NEW JERSEY — On the first floor of American Dream, a sprawling retail complex in New Jersey near New York's Manhattan, a K-brand pop-up store opened on the 14th to a steady stream of influencers and shoppers eager to try Korean cosmetics, food and K-pop idol merchandise. The store was set up by Chungdam Global, a South Korean distribution company, with support from the Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA). Visitors peppered staff with questions about the products and dabbed cosmetics onto their faces and hands, exclaiming as they went. Young fans of the K-pop acts BTS and Seventeen crowded around Christmas stockings designed after individual members. Zea, a TikTok influencer who was at the store, said American skin care often triggers breakouts for her. "I've never had that happen once with Korean products, so I really love them," she said. "Korean products have the best moisturizing power and good sun protection, so I filmed all of my reactions on video."
 A middle-aged man applies Korean cosmetics to his face at a K-brand pop-up store set up by KOTRA and Korean distributor Chungdam Global at American Dream Mall, a large mixed-use shopping complex in New Jersey, on Nov. 14 local time. New Jersey — Yoon Kyung-hwan, Correspondent Chungdam Global and KOTRA opened the pop-up to promote products from South Korean small and midsize companies to high-spending consumers on the U.S. East Coast, timed to Black Friday on the 27th of this month, Christmas on Dec. 25 and the start of next year — the peak of the American shopping calendar. It is also the first K-brand pop-up on the East Coast for Kreassive, Chungdam Global's U.S. subsidiary, which is based in Los Angeles. "We had been running pop-up stores only in California, on the West Coast, and we are looking for an opportunity to expand to the East," said Sean Chang, co-chief executive of Kreassive.
 A total of 58 brands are on display, including 49 in K-beauty and nine in K-food. Of those, 18 are brands from South Korean small and midsize companies — 10 in beauty and eight in food. Sixteen of the brands are showing their products in a U.S. brick-and-mortar store for the first time, including the basic skin care maker DAMTIX, the sun care company SIABARRIER, the fragrance and hand cream brand KEYTH, the konjac jelly maker DR.LIV and the gochujang sauce company SAUCECO.
 Young shoppers browse K-pop idol merchandise at a K-brand pop-up store set up by KOTRA and Korean distributor Chungdam Global at American Dream Mall, a large mixed-use shopping complex in New Jersey, on Nov. 14 local time. New Jersey — Yoon Kyung-hwan, Correspondent KOTRA and Chungdam Global plan to run the pop-up from that day through Jan. 15 of next year. The store will sell about 18,000 units across roughly 200 product lines, along with some 1,300 kinds of official merchandise from more than 40 K-pop acts. Over the 63-day run, the two organizations are targeting 36,000 visitors, or an average of about 570 a day, 8,900 paying customers, sales of 17,900 units and revenue of $260,000. They expect 13% of revenue to come during Black Friday week and 22% between Dec. 14 and 25, just before Christmas.
 Na Beom-geun, head of KOTRA's New York office, said the year-end season, when consumer spending is most concentrated, is a good chance for smaller brands to gauge local reaction firsthand. "Rent and staffing costs make it hard for an individual small or midsize company to run its own store in the United States, so we will use the sales records built at this pop-up to connect them with local buyers," he said. Carol Feng, co-chief executive of Kreassive, said young K-pop fans understand Korean products well. "This event is a great platform for American consumers to discover Korean culture," she said.
 Influencers and shoppers try out Korean cosmetics at a K-brand pop-up store set up by KOTRA and Korean distributor Chungdam Global at American Dream Mall, a large mixed-use shopping complex in New Jersey, on Nov. 14 local time. New Jersey — Yoon Kyung-hwan, Correspondent # KBeauty # KPop # KOTRA # AmericanDream # BlackFriday # KFood # Skincare Original reporting by Yoon Kyoung-hwan for Seoul Economic Daily.
